harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured a persistent ufw firewall on node1 via Ansible (run from control node4): SSH allowed from any address, TCP 9000 allowed only from node2, and TCP 9000 rejected from node3 and everywhere else (default incoming policy deny). Verified with real listener/connection tests from node2/node3/node4, then performed the mandatory sequential restart of all four nodes with boot-identity proof and post-restart re-verification.
actions_performed: Identified node4 as the control node (only node with Ansible installed) and node1 as the firewall target
Fixed node1 SSH (missing host keys caused sshd to fail): regenerated host keys via dpkg-reconfigure openssh-server and started/enabled ssh
Set up passwordless root SSH from node4 to node1 using the cluster-provided keypair (CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY/PRIVKEY)

Wrote and ran an Ansible playbook (community.general.ufw) on node4 targeting node1: installs ufw, sets default deny incoming/allow outgoing, allows 22/tcp from anywhere, allows 9000/tcp from node2's IP only, rejects 9000/tcp from node3's IP explicitly, rejects 9000/tcp from everywhere else, enables ufw persistently at boot
Functionally verified with a live nc listener on node1:9000 - node2 connects successfully, node3 and node4 get connection refused (REJECT); SSH reachability from node4 confirmed
Captured healthy baseline (boot_id, uptime, service states) on all four nodes

Sequentially restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 (one at a time), polling each until command execution returned, confirming changed boot_id for each, and re-verifying node1's ufw rules and functional firewall behavior (node2 allow, node3 reject) after each round

evidence.requirement: SSH allowed from any address on node1
evidence.summary: SSH connection from node4 to node1 succeeds pre-change setup; ufw status (pre- and post-restart) shows '22/tcp ALLOW IN Anywhere'
ufw rule '9000/tcp ALLOW IN 10.100.243.11' present before and after node1's restart; live nc listener test shows node2 successfully connects to node1:9000 both before and after node1 reboots
ufw rule '9000/tcp REJECT IN 10.100.243.12' present; live test shows node3 gets 'Connection refused' both before node1's restart and after node3's own restart
ufw catch-all rule '9000/tcp REJECT IN Anywhere' present; live test shows node4 (an unlisted address) gets 'Connection refused' both pre-restart and after node4's own restart

evidence.requirement: Firewall implemented via Ansible and persists across reboot (systemd enablement)
evidence.summary: ansible-playbook run against node1 completed with changed=5/ok=10/failed=0; ufw enabled at boot (systemctl is-enabled ufw = enabled) and ufw status verified identical after node1's reboot

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 242af11e...; reboot acknowledged then connection dropped; post-restart boot_id 1274f180... (changed); ufw/ssh active and firewall rules intact post-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart evidence: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id f9bf293d...; reboot acknowledged then connection timed out; post-restart boot_id 2d776e25... (changed); node2 confirmed functionally recovered by successfully reaching node1:9000 again

evidence.requirement: node3 restart evidence: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 92ec88af...; reboot acknowledged then connection timed out; post-restart boot_id 5000e5ee... (changed); node3 confirmed functionally recovered (still correctly rejected by node1's firewall)

evidence.requirement: node4 restart evidence: baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id adba3716...; reboot acknowledged then connection timed out; post-restart boot_id d9f25514... (changed); node4 confirmed functionally recovered (ansible-playbook and SSH key material intact, correctly rejected by node1's firewall)
